title: From my_gen_server to OTP gen_server & Live sys:get_state/1 Introspection
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates OTP Inversion of Control with gen_server callbacks and live state inspection via sys:get_state/1 without taking down the process.

otpDocCards.description: Spawns a gen_server linked to the caller, synchronously invoking Mod:init(Args).
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) process creation with atomic link.

otpDocCards.description: Synchronously queries the internal state of a process implementing OTP system messages.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is writing raw spawn and receive loops considered an anti-pattern in production Erlang systems?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% Raw Process Loop:
loop(State) ->
    receive Msg -> loop(handle(Msg, State)) end.

options.label: Raw loops fail to handle standard OTP system messages, breaking supervisor shutdowns, live sys:get_state/1 inspection, and hot code upgrades.
options.explanation: Correct! An OTP gen_server handles supervisor signals, live tracing, sys introspection, and code_change/3 out of the box, whereas raw loops silently ignore or break on system protocol messages.

options.label: Raw spawn loops consume 100x more RAM than gen_server processes.
options.explanation: Both use standard BEAM processes with ~2.5 KB initial heap.

options.label: Erlang prevents modules from compiling if they use spawn.
options.explanation: spawn/1 and spawn/3 are standard built-in functions, but OTP provides higher-level abstractions.
